<!-- head-1: body_md -->
If the flat dimension of $L_{B/A}$ as a $B$-module is finite, and the flat dimension of $B$
as an $A$-module is finite, then $f$ is locally complete intersection. In particular, the
flat dimension of $L_{B/A}$ is less than or equal to one.
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- head-2: body_md -->
Drop the assumption that $B$ is of finite flat dimension as an $A$-module from
the first conjecture. Then the flat dimension of $L_{B/A}$ is less than or equal to
two.
<!-- end head-2 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:intro}
Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of noetherian rings of characteristic
$2$ with $\operatorname{fd}_B L_{B/A}<\infty$. Then $\operatorname{fd}_B L_{B/A}\leq 2$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:turner}
Let $X$ be a connected augmented simplicial commutative $\ell$-algebra
such that $\bigoplus_iH^{Q}_i(X)$ is finite-dimensional. If
$\vartheta=\alpha_1$ acts nilpotently on the indecomposables $Q\pi_*X$, then
$H^{Q}_i(X)=0$ for $i\geq 3$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
While the notation $\vartheta$ is a clever reindexing, it is important to
    keep in mind that the iterates $\vartheta^N$ change degree in each
    iteration. If we for instance start with a degree three class $x_3$,
    the iterates are
    $$
        x_3\xrightarrow{\delta_2}x_5\xrightarrow{\delta_4}x_9
        \xrightarrow{\delta_8}x_{17}\longrightarrow\cdots.
    $$
    In this example the words describing the iterated operation are powers of
    two.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:filtration}
Let $R$ be a simplicial algebra and $L_1\supseteq L_2\supseteq\cdots$
simplicial ideals with $L_pL_q\subseteq L_{p+q}$. Then
$\Theta_i(C(L_q)_n)\subseteq C(L_{2q})_{n+i}$ for $1\leq i\leq n$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The maps $\Delta^k$ are natural in the simplicial vector spaces, so they
take $C(L_q)\otimes C(L_q)$ into $C(L_q\otimes L_q)$. The differential
preserves $C(L_q)$, and $\mu$ maps $L_q\otimes L_q$ into
$L_qL_q\subseteq L_{2q}$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:boundary}
Let $R$ be a simplicial algebra, let $L\subseteq R$ be a simplicial
ideal, and put $X=R/L$. Write
$\beta\colon\pi_mX\to\pi_{m-1}L$ for the boundary homomorphisms
associated to the exact sequence of underlying simplicial vector spaces
\[
  0\longrightarrow L\longrightarrow R\longrightarrow X\longrightarrow0.
\]
For every $\xi\in\pi_mX$ with $m\geq3$ and every $N\geq0$, one has
\begin{equation}\label{eq:boundary-operations}
  \beta(\vartheta^N\xi)=\gamma_2^N\beta(\xi)
  \qquad\text{in }\pi_{2^N(m-1)}L.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Let $w\in C(X)_m$ be a cycle representing $\xi$, and choose a lift
$u\in C(R)_m$. Then $v=\partial u$ is a cycle in $C(L)_{m-1}$
representing $\beta(\xi)$. By naturality, $\vartheta^N(u)$ lifts the
cycle $\vartheta^N(w)$ representing $\vartheta^N\xi$. Equation
\eqref{eq:iterate} therefore gives
\[
  \beta(\vartheta^N\xi)
  =[\partial\vartheta^N(u)]
  =[\gamma_2^N(v)]
  =\gamma_2^N\beta(\xi).
\]
Here the brackets denote homology classes in $C(L)$. The degrees agree
since $\vartheta^N\xi$ has degree $1+2^N(m-1)$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:nilpotence}
Let $R$ be a simplicial algebra, let
$L_1\supseteq L_2\supseteq\cdots$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:filtration}, and
put $X=R/L_1$. Assume the connecting homomorphism $\beta: \pi_d X \to \pi_{d-1}
L_1$ is injective for $d \geq 3$. Suppose $b\geq 0$ is such that $L_q\to L_1$ induces zero on
homotopy for every $q>b$. Then $\vartheta^N=0$ on $\pi_mX$ for all
$m\geq 3$ and all $N$ with $2^N>b$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Let $\xi\in\pi_mX$ with $m\geq3$, and let $N$ satisfy $2^N>b$.
By
Lemmas~\ref{lem:boundary} and~\ref{lem:filtration},
\[
  \beta(\vartheta^N\xi)
  =\gamma_2^N\beta(\xi).
\]
Since $2^N > b$, we know that the right hand side lies in
\[
 \operatorname{im}\!\left(
    \pi_{d-1}L_{2^N}\longrightarrow\pi_{d-1}L_1
  \right),
\]
and thus is zero.
Injectivity of $\beta$
gives $\vartheta^N\xi=0$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:quillen}
Let $P$ be a simplicial algebra with polynomial terms $P_n$, and let
$J\subseteq P$ be a simplicial ideal such that $J_n$ is generated by
a subset of the polynomial generators of $P_n$ and $\pi_0J=0$. Then
$J^q\in(\operatorname{Mod}_P)_{\geq q}$ for all $q\geq 1$. Consequently, if
$\pi_iJ=0$ for $i>b$, the inclusion $J^q\toJ$ is nullhomotopic in
$\operatorname{Mod}_P$ for all $q>b$.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Each $J_n$ is a regular ideal, so the first assertion is Quillen's
convergence theorem. See the proof of \cite[Proposition 4.11]{bhatt-completions}
for a modern reference. The second assertion
follows since $J\in(\operatorname{Mod}_P)_{\leq b}$ and $q>b$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:bounded}
Let $E$ be a simplicial algebra with an augmentation $E\to\ell$, put
$S=\pi_0E$, and suppose $\pi_iE=0$ for $i>b$. Then
$\vartheta^N=0$ on $\pi_m(S\otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_E\ell)$ for all $m\geq 3$ and all $N$
with $2^N>b$.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
The map $E\to S$ is degreewise surjective, since $E_0\to\pi_0E$ is
surjective and factors through every $E_n$ via a degeneracy. Let $J$ be
its kernel. Then $\pi_0J=0$ and $\pi_iJ\cong\pi_iE$ for $i\geq 1$, so
$\pi_iJ=0$ for $i>b$. Choose a cofibrant replacement
$(P,I)\to(E,J)$ in the model category of pairs consisting of a
simplicial algebra and a simplicial ideal, defined over $\mathbb{F}_2$ exactly as
over $\mathbb Z$ in \cite[proof of Corollary 4.14]{bhatt-completions}:
each $P_n$ is a polynomial algebra, $I_n$ is generated by a subset of
its polynomial generators, and $P\to E$ and $I\to J$, hence also
$P/I\to S$, are weak equivalences. By Proposition~\ref{prop:quillen},
$I^q\to I$ is nullhomotopic in $\operatorname{Mod}_P$ for $q>b$.

Factor $P\to E\to\ell$ as $P\to R\to\ell$, an almost free map followed
by a trivial fibration \cite[Proposition 1.4]{goerss186}. Each $R_n$ is a
polynomial $P_n$-algebra, hence flat over $P_n$. Using a result of Illusie
\cite[Lemme 3.3.2.1]{illusie}, 
we obtain 
$M\otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_PR\simeq M\otimes_PR$, naturally in $M$.

Put $L_q=I^qR$. By
flatness, $L_q=I^q\otimes_PR$, so $L_q=L_1^q$, $L_pL_q=L_{p+q}$. By Illusie's
lemma, 
$L_q\to L_1$ is the base change of $I^q\to I$ along $P\to R$, hence
nullhomotopic in $\operatorname{Mod}_R$ for $q>b$. Moreover $\pi_iR=0$ for $i>0$.

Finally $R/L_1=(P/I)\otimes_PR$. If $Q\to P/I$ is a cofibrant
replacement of $P$-algebras, then $Q\otimes_PR$ computes the homotopy
pushout $(P/I)\otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_PR$ because $R$ is cofibrant over $P$, and
$Q\otimes_PR\to(P/I)\otimes_PR$ is a weak equivalence by the previous
paragraph. Using the weak equivalences $P\to E$, $P/I\to S$ and
$R\to\ell$, we obtain
\[
  R/L_1\simeq(P/I)\otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_PR\simeq S\otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_E\ell
\]
as simplicial algebras. As $\pi_i(R)=0$ for $i >0$, the connecting morphism
$\beta$ in the sequence $L_1 \to R \to R/L_1$ is automatically injective from
$i >2$. Thus Proposition~\ref{prop:nilpotence}, applied to
$R$, the ideals $L_q$ and $X=R/L_1$, gives the claim.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rem:derived-ideal-filtration}
For the readers not so accustomed to model categories and explicit simplicial
resolutions, we sketch a different argument based on the ideals developed by
\cite{hekking}.  The central inputs remain Quillen's connectivity theorem and
the boundary compatibility with higher divided powers. To me it is not
immediately clear that Quillen's connectivity theorem applies to the ideal
powers of \cite{hekking}, so this is not an alternative proof.

Keeping the notation and assumptions from Theorem \ref{thm:bounded},
put $D=S\otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_E\ell$ and let $\mathcal{J}=\operatorname{fib}(E\to S)$, regarded
as a derived ideal of $E$. Write $\mathcal{J}^{[q]}$ for its derived powers as defined
in \cite[\S~3.2]{hekking}. We use brackets to distinguish these powers from
ordinary degreewise powers. 
Define
\[
  \mathcal{K}_q=\mathcal{J}^{[q]}\otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_E\ell,
  \qquad
  D_q=(E/\mathcal{J}^{[q]})\otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_E\ell.
\]
Compatibility of derived ideal powers with base change
\cite[Remark~4.6.9]{hekking} identifies $\mathcal{K}_q$ with the $q$-th derived
power of $\mathcal{K}=\operatorname{fib}(\ell\to D)$ and $D_q$ with the derived
quotient $\ell/\mathcal{K}_q$. In particular, $\mathcal{K}_1=\mathcal{K}$, $D_1=D$, and there is a
tower of augmented algebras
\[
  \cdots\longrightarrow D_3\longrightarrow D_2\longrightarrow D_1=D.
\]
For $m\geq2$, this gives a decreasing filtration 
\[
  F^q\pi_mD
  :=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\pi_mD_q\longrightarrow\pi_mD\bigr),
  \qquad F^1\pi_mD=\pi_mD.
\]
Since $\ell$ is discrete, the boundary maps of the underlying module
fibre sequences are isomorphisms
\[
  \beta_q:\pi_mD_q\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_{m-1}\mathcal{K}_q,
\]
thus identifying the filtration with
\[
  F^q\pi_mD
  =\beta^{-1}\!\left(
    \operatorname{im}\bigl(\pi_{m-1}\mathcal{K}_q\longrightarrow\pi_{m-1}\mathcal{K}\bigr)
  \right).
\]
Assuming that Quillen's connectivity holds for the powers $\mathcal{J}^{[q]}$
and using that $\mathcal{J}$ is truncated,
we get
\[
F^q\pi_mD=0\qquad(q>b,\ m\geq2).
\]
Finally, the boundary identity \eqref{eq:iterate} gives us
\[
\vartheta\bigl(F^q\pi_mD\bigr)
\subseteq F^{2q}\pi_{2m-1}D.
\]
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:AQ}
There are isomorphisms $H^{Q}_i(D)\cong\mathrm{D}_i(S|A;\ell)$ for $i\geq 3$.
If, in addition, \(\bigoplus_i \mathrm{D}_i(S|A;\ell)\) is finite-dimensional,
then \(\bigoplus_i H^{Q}_i(D)\) is finite-dimensional.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
The transitivity triangle of $A\to E\to S$, tensored with $\ell$ over $S$,
is
\[
  L_{E/A}\otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_E\ell\longrightarrow L_{S/A}\otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_S\ell\longrightarrow
  L_{S/E}\otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_S\ell.
\]
Since $E$ is quasi-smooth over $A$ \cite{elmanto}, the first term is $\ell^c[1]$, a shifted sum
of finite copies of $\ell$. By base change along
$E\to\ell$, we have $L_{D/\ell}\simeq L_{S/E}\otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_SD$, so the last term is
$L_{D/\ell}\otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_D\ell$. The long exact sequence of homotopy groups
gives the claim.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:main}
Let $A$ be a noetherian local ring over a field $\ell$ of characteristic
$2$, I an ideal in $A$, and $S=A/I$. If $\mathrm{D}_i(S|A;\ell)=0$ for $i\gg 0$, then
$\mathrm{D}_i(S|A;\ell)=0$ for all $i\geq 3$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
As above, set  $E=A//(f_1, \dots, f_c)$, and let $D$ be the difference algebra
    associated to $A \to S$.  Set the bound $b$ needed in
    Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded} to $b=c$. By \eqref{eq:bounded}, $E \to S$
    satisfies the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:bounded}, and we conclude that
    $\vartheta^N$ is nilpotent on $\pi_{\geq 3} D$, and thus also the induced
    operation on $Q\pi_*D$ is nilpotent.

    By Lemma~\ref{lem:AQ}, $\bigoplus_iH^{Q}_i(D)$ is finite-dimensional, allowing us
    to apply Turner's criterion  Theorem~\ref{thm:turner} and deduce $H^{Q}_i(D)=0$
    for $i\geq 3$. Finally, using Lemma~\ref{lem:AQ} again we can shift the result
    from $D$ over $\ell$ to $S$ over $A$.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
Equivalently, the theorem can be stated using flat dimension. More
    precisely, the statement is: if $\operatorname{fd}_SL_{S/A}<\infty$ then $\operatorname{fd}_SL_{S/A}\leq
    2$. This holds since, as $A$ is noetherian, $L_{S/A}$ is quasi-isomorphic to
    a bounded-below complex of finitely generated free $S$-modules. Hence each
    $\mathrm{D}_i(S|A;\ell)$ is finite-dimensional and
    $\operatorname{fd}_SL_{S/A}=\sup\{i\mid\mathrm{D}_i(S|A;\ell)\neq 0\}$.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:global}
Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of noetherian rings of characteristic
$2$ with $\operatorname{fd}_BL_{B/A}<\infty$. Then $\operatorname{fd}_BL_{B/A}\leq 2$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
We argue as in the proof of \cite[Theorem D]{turner}. Let $q\in\operatorname{Spec} B$ and let
$p\in\operatorname{Spec} A$ be its contraction. By \cite{avramov-foxby-herzog} there is a
Cohen factorisation $\widehat A_p\to A'\to\widehat B_q$ with $A'$ a complete
local ring, $\widehat A_p\to A'$ flat with regular closed fibre, and
$A'\to\widehat B_q$ surjective. By \cite[\S 1]{avramov}, one has
$\operatorname{fd}_BL_{B/A}\leq n$ if and only if $\mathrm{D}_s(\widehat B_q|A';k(q))=0$ for all $s>n$
and all $q\in\operatorname{Spec} B$. As $A'$ has characteristic $2$, Theorem~\ref{thm:main}
applies to $A'\to\widehat B_q$ and gives the claim.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
